scenes.tts: What happens to a person when proprioceptive input is lost?
scenes.visual: Title card: When the Line Goes Quiet. A stretch line drawn as a wire that fades to grey.
scenes.narration: What happens to a person when proprioceptive input is lost?

scenes.tts: Picture reaching for a cup in a lit room, with your stretch lines silent.
scenes.visual: Stylised arm reaching toward a cup in a lit room. No faces.
scenes.narration: Picture reaching for a cup in a lit room, with your stretch lines silent.

scenes.tts: Predict. What would you have to rely on to know where your arm is?
scenes.visual: Question on screen: what does most of the work for the silent line?
scenes.narration: Predict. What would you have to rely on to know where your arm is?

scenes.tts: Mainly your eyes. Vision does much of the work. Take it away too, and reaching becomes far less accurate.
scenes.visual: An eye icon lights up beside the arm; then the room light goes off and the reach veers off the cup.
scenes.narration: Mainly your eyes. Vision does much of the work. Take it away too, and reaching becomes far less accurate.

scenes.tts: Chesler and colleagues reported two unrelated young people with inactivating variants in both copies of Piezo two.
scenes.caption: Chesler and colleagues reported two unrelated young people with inactivating variants in both copies of PIEZO2.
scenes.visual: Text card: Chesler and colleagues, 2016. Two people with inactivating PIEZO2 variants in both copies.
scenes.narration: Chesler and colleagues reported two unrelated young people with inactivating variants in both copies of PIEZO2.

scenes.tts: Reaching was tested with and without sight. Without vision, their uncoordinated movements and misjudged reaches became markedly worse.
scenes.visual: Two reach paths: with sight, close to the target; sight blocked, wide and overshooting. Labels: ataxia; dysmetria.
scenes.narration: Reaching was tested with and without sight. Without vision, their uncoordinated movements and misjudged reaches became markedly worse.

scenes.tts: Yet they could still walk, talk and write, though one walked only with support.
scenes.visual: Three simple icons: walking, talking, writing. A small note: one walked only with support.
scenes.narration: Yet they could still walk, talk and write, though one walked only with support.

scenes.tts: An older case shows the daily cost. A man known as I W had lost large-fibre sensation below the neck.
scenes.caption: An older case shows the daily cost. A man known as I.W. had lost large-fibre sensation below the neck.
scenes.visual: Text card: I.W., Cole and Sedgwick, 1992. A body outline shaded below the neck.
scenes.narration: An older case shows the daily cost. A man known as I.W. had lost large-fibre sensation below the neck.

scenes.tts: He lacked light touch and position sense. But he kept pain, temperature and the sense of muscle fatigue.
scenes.visual: Two lists: lost, light touch and proprioception; kept, pain, heat, cold, fatigue.
scenes.narration: He lacked light touch and position sense. But he kept pain, temperature and the sense of muscle fatigue.

scenes.tts: In testing, he could make no new movement without watching it. Every new movement had to be watched.
scenes.visual: A hand moves only while an eye icon follows it; when the eye closes, the new movement stops.
scenes.narration: In testing, he could make no new movement without watching it. Every new movement had to be watched.

scenes.tts: Both cases show the rule's second half. With proprioceptive input lost, accurate movement depends heavily on vision. Neither case silences spindles alone; touch was affected too.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card, second half highlighted: with proprioceptive input lost, accurate movement depends heavily on vision. Small note: neither case silences spindles alone.
scenes.narration: Both cases show the rule's second half. With proprioceptive input lost, accurate movement depends heavily on vision. Neither case silences spindles alone; touch was affected too.

scenes.tts: In mice, the line turned out to matter for the skeleton too.
scenes.visual: A mouse spine silhouette appears beside a spindle icon.
scenes.narration: In mice, the line turned out to matter for the skeleton too.

scenes.tts: Deleting Piezo two with a parvalbumin driver curved the spine in some mice by postnatal day sixty.
scenes.caption: Deleting Piezo2 with a parvalbumin driver curved the spine in some mice by postnatal day 60.
scenes.visual: CT-style spine silhouettes: control straight; Pvalb-Cre-targeted Piezo2 deletion with a single C-shaped curve. Label: P60, some animals.
scenes.narration: Deleting Piezo2 with a parvalbumin driver curved the spine in some mice by postnatal day 60.

scenes.tts: Deleting it in bone and cartilage lineages did not curve the spine, at the ages tested.
scenes.visual: A third silhouette, straight. Card: Col1a1-Cre and Col2a1-Cre, no spinal curve at the ages tested.
scenes.narration: Deleting it in bone and cartilage lineages did not curve the spine, at the ages tested.

scenes.tts: The authors read this as non-autonomous. The curve shows in the skeleton, but the gene was lost in parvalbumin-labelled neurons.
scenes.visual: Arrow from a parvalbumin-labelled sensory neuron to the spine. Label: non-autonomous, the authors' interpretation: defect in one tissue, gene lost in another.
scenes.narration: The authors read this as non-autonomous. The curve shows in the skeleton, but the gene was lost in parvalbumin-labelled neurons.

scenes.tts: How the signal reaches the skeleton is not known.
scenes.visual: The arrow becomes dashed, with a question mark on it.
scenes.narration: How the signal reaches the skeleton is not known.

scenes.tts: One limit to remember. Near a joint's limits, and for the feeling of effort, the stretch rule is not the whole story.
scenes.visual: Two limit cards: joint limits, where joint and skin afferents fire; force and effort, where tendon organs and effort contribute.
scenes.narration: One limit to remember. Near a joint's limits, and for the feeling of effort, the stretch rule is not the whole story.

scenes.tts: So limb position is an estimate built mainly from the stretch line. Lose that input, and vision does much of its work.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: position is an estimate built mainly from the stretch line; lose that input, and vision does much of its work.
scenes.narration: So limb position is an estimate built mainly from the stretch line. Lose that input, and vision does much of its work.
